tools.name: check_url
tools.description: FREE: preflight target URL safety and pricing

tools.name: scrape_markdown
tools.description: PAID $0.005 USDC (x402, Base): URL to clean markdown. Over MCP this returns payment requirements; settle by calling POST /v1/scrape/markdown with x402 payment headers.

tools.name: extract_structured
tools.description: PAID $0.02 USDC (x402, Base): URL plus JSON schema to structured JSON. Over MCP this returns payment requirements; settle by calling POST /v1/extract with x402 payment headers.

tools.name: compare_market_rules
tools.description: PAID $0.05 USDC (x402, Base): Compare Polymarket rules with a bookmaker market description. Over MCP this returns payment requirements; settle by calling POST /v1/market-rules/compare with x402 payment headers.

tools.name: page_changed
tools.description: PAID $0.003 USDC (x402, Base): Whether a page changed since a hash or timestamp. Over MCP this returns payment requirements; settle by calling POST /v1/page/changed with x402 payment headers.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_url, scrape_markdown · Public sink: scrape_markdown, extract_structured, compare_market_rules, page_changed.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_url, scrape_markdown · Public sink: scrape_markdown, extract_structured, compare_market_rules, page_changed

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
